chapter: Trombonists and bandleaders across the river
title: Buddy Johnson's society band versus rough barrelhouse bands
summary: Buddy Johnson led a big-time musical band, in contrast to Frankie Duson's rough barrelhouse band; both Johnsons were around when Valentine arrived.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Do you remember his brother's band? And Fess tells us about Buddy Johnson, like he had sort of a society band.
And in the old days, Frankie Doosen had sort of a rough, you know, ratty band.
That played for the barrel house style. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Buddy Johnson had a, what you call it, what you call it, a big time, you know.
How long was Buddy Johnson around? Was he still playing when you started across the river? Sure he was playing. He was still there then.
Yank was playing, Orlenfeld was there when I came here, when we had our band.
I never knew any of them, I don't even know when they died or how long they were here.
